tools.name: register
tools.description: Start signing a person up. Sends a sign-in email to their work address. No API key needed. Ask the person for their own work email and name first. Personal addresses such as gmail.com are refused. The email holds a code, a sign-in link or both. Ask the person for the code, or to copy the link WITHOU

tools.name: confirm_registration
tools.description: Finish signing up with the code from the email, or with the sign-in link copied from it unopened. Returns the person's API key, shown once, and how to connect with it. Save the key in the MCP connection's settings as the Authorization header, then reconnect to get the full set of tools.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "confirm_registration" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "confirm_registration" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: confirm_registration · Private data: register, confirm_registration · Public sink: register, confirm_registration.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: confirm_registration · Private data: register, confirm_registration · Public sink: register, confirm_registration

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
